why_hard: Weight management comes up everywhere: yearly PCP counseling, self-joined Weight Watchers, and a dietitian education visit. None of it is a supervised medical weight-loss program with a duration and result.

pages.title: Bariatric surgery consultation
lines: PMH: HTN (2010), T2DM (2019, metformin), L knee replacement 2022.
Weight hx: has been unable to lose weight despite years of dieting and physician counseling.

pages.title: Primary care notes (excerpts)
lines: MEADOWBROOK PRIMARY CARE - Bauer, Clementine A.
06/12/2024 annual: BMI elevated. Counseled on diet and exercise, handout given. Pt says she did Weight Watchers on her own in 2019 - lost 12 lb, regained.
06/18/2025 annual: weight up 6 lb. Discussed weight management; advised Mediterranean diet and walking. Pt not interested in meds.
06/10/2026 annual: weight management discussed again. Pt now interested in surgery. Referral placed.

pages.title: Dietitian education visit
lines: Reviewed post-RYGB diet stages, protein targets, vitamins. Pt understands.
Weight today 252 lb. No weight-loss program enrollment at this time.

pages.title: Surgical plan
lines: Expected LOS: 2 midnights. Factors: T2DM, HTN, age 63 with prior knee arthroplasty and VTE risk.

prior_medical_treatment.why: No supervised medical weight-loss program is documented. Yearly PCP counseling is advice, not a program. Weight Watchers 2019 was self-joined and commercial. The dietitian visit was one-time surgical education and states 'No weight-loss program enrollment'.

action_reasoning: Rule 3 needs documented supervised medical treatment that failed. It is absent. Pend. Other rules pass.
